settings.name_in_paper: Transductive linear bandits (pure exploration, fixed confidence)
unmapped: Transductive: measurement set X differs from item set Z; goal is argmax over Z of z^T theta* while measuring only x in X
settings.definition_quote: Consider known finite collections of $d$-dimensional vectors $\calX\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $ \calZ\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ , known confidence $\delta\in(0,1)$, and unknown $\theta^{\ast}\in \mathbb{R}^d$. The objective is to identify $z_{\ast} = \argmax_{z\in \calZ} z^{\top}\theta^{\ast}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ while taking as few measurements in $\mc{X}$ as possible. ... $\eta_t$ is independent, zero-mean, and 1-sub-Gaussian.

symbols.psi_star: min over designs lambda on X of max over z != z* of ||z*-z||^2_{A(lambda)^{-1}} / ((z*-z)^T theta*)^2

source.label: thm:LowerBound
source.quote: Assume $\eta_t \overset{iid}{\sim} \calN(0,1)$ for all $t$. Then for any $\delta\in (0,1)$, any $\delta$-PAC algorithm must satisfy \E_{\theta^\ast}[\tau] \geq \log(1/2.4\delta)\min_{\lambda\in \simplex_{\calX}}\max_{z\in \calZ\setminus \{z_{\ast}\}} \frac{\|z_{\ast} - z\|^2_{(\sum_{x\in \calX} \lambda_x x x^\top)^{-1}}}{((z_\ast-z)^\top\theta^{\ast})^2}.

results.notes: Applies to delta-PAC algorithms; algorithm_class set to other (delta-PAC). Generalizes Soare and combinatorial lower bounds.

symbols.gamma_p: free parameter gamma > 0 of the construction; on the instance psi*/c' <= d + 1/gamma

conditions: X = Z specific construction with set Theta
algorithm class: delta-PAC algorithms using a static (non-adaptive) allocation

source.label: prop:fixedLowerBound
source.quote: Let $c,c'$ be universal constants. For any $\gamma > 0$, $d$ even, there exists sets $\calX=\calZ \subset \mb{R}^d$ and a set $\Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\inf_{\mc{A}}\max_{\theta\in \Theta} \E_\theta[\tau] \geq \frac{c d\log(1/\delta)}{\gamma}$ where $\mc{A}$ is the set of all algorithms that are $\delta$-PAC for $\mc{X},\mc{Z}$ and take a static allocation of samples. On the other hand $\psi^{\ast}/c'\leq  d+\frac{1}{\gamma}$ for every choice of $\theta^\ast \in \Theta$.

results.notes: Lower bound for static allocations only; shows factor d gap versus psi*. c is a universal constant (mapped to c_alg).

symbols.rho_S: rho(Y(S_t)) = min_lambda max_{y in Y(S_t)} ||y||^2_{A(lambda)^{-1}}, S_t = {z: Delta(z) <= 2^{-t}}
symbols.r_eps: minimum number of samples r(epsilon) for the rounding procedure (O(d/eps^2))

source.label: thm:SampleComplexity
source.quote: With probability greater than $1-\delta$, using an $\epsilon$-efficient rounding procedure, Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} correctly identifies the optimal arm $z_*$ and requires a worst-case sample complexity \[\randnumsamples \leq \sum_{\phaseindex=1}^{\lfloor \log_2(1/\Delta_{\min}) \rfloor} \max\big\{8 \big\lceil (2^{\phaseindex+1})^2 \rho(\yset(\sset_{\phaseindex}))(1+ \epsilon)\log(\phaseindex^2|\calZ|^2/\delta)\big\rceil, r(\epsilon)\big\}\] ...

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1-delta jointly with correct identification. Paper's 8 placement outside the ceiling kept as in theorem statement.

symbols.r_eps: rounding minimum sample count r(epsilon), can be O(d/eps^2)

source.label: thm:SampleComplexity
source.quote: Furthermore, $N \leq c \psi^{\ast}\log(1/\Delta_{\min})\log(|\calZ|^2\log(1/\Delta_{\min})^2/\delta)+r(\epsilon)\log_2(1/\Delta_{\min})$ for some absolute constant $c$, in other words Algorithm \ref{alg:main} is instance optimal up to logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Absolute constant c on first term absorbed into O notation; proof gives 128(1+eps). Matches Theorem 1 lower bound up to log factors.
